rules.title: Prohibition on Sale or Use of Coordinated Pricing Algorithms
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to sell, license, or provide to Berkeley landlords, or for a landlord to use, a 'coordinated pricing algorithm' that uses nonpublic competitor data (actual rents, occupancy rates, lease dates, etc., less than 90 days old) to set or recommend rents, fees, occupancy rates, or other lease terms for residential dwelling units in coordination with the landlord's competitors.

coverage_conditions.notes: Applies to all residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley; no building-age, unit-count, or ownership-type limits stated.

rules.exemptions: Does not apply to: products that only publish aggregated, anonymous rental data without recommending rents/fees/occupancy; products used to set rent or income limits under affordable housing guidelines of a government; products/processes used for market research for project financing, appraisals, or software research/testing/training (so long as the data is not used as a live input when a recommendation is calculated for a Berkeley landlord). The Chapter does not itself regulate the amount of rent a landlord may charge.
rules.interaction: This Chapter regulates only the use and sale of coordinated pricing algorithms; it does not set or cap rent amounts, which are governed separately by other Berkeley/state rent regulations.
rules.penalty: Civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation (each month of violation and each unit is a separate violation), plus damages, injunctive relief, and restitution/return of illegal profits; enforceable by the City Attorney (both subsections) or by an aggrieved tenant (for landlord-use violations), with mandatory attorney's fees and costs to the prevailing enforcing party/tenant.
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm described in subsection A when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.
rules.conflict_note: The ordinance is captioned 'Ordinance No. 7,992-N.S.' (suggesting adoption) but the body text states only that it 'was passed to print and ordered published' at the November 18, 2025 Council meeting; no explicit effective date is given in this document, so the precise in-force date is not fully clear from the text alone.
